title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: No prior price increase; past promotions show limited lift even at 30% off. Price sensitivity evident in 2026-08-31 (14 units after high volume). Noise-adjusted estimate suggests modest demand drop.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median of 14.7 is already elevated by the ongoing back-to-school season (recent weeks 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-24 averaged 39.5 units). The price increase to $9.03 (+2.3%) is a known demand reducer. Past promotions show a noise-adjusted lift of x1.15, but the 30% off in April (x2.86) was exceptional and not replicable here. No event or promotion is scheduled. The classical uplift model's x1.00 is consistent with no driver. The price hike likely suppresses demand. Evidence for a price effect is limited to one past price change (no prior increase), so the effect is uncertain. Shrink toward 1.0.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-65% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
